title.narrative: Disability Inclusion for Women and Girls FIRST Phase II Project

description.narrative:
CAFOD Sierra Leone is implementing a three-year Women and Girls FIRST Phase II project, funded by JOA, aimed at enhancing financial inclusion and strengthening livelihood resilience among rural communities—particularly women and girls—in five remote districts of Sierra Leone. An evaluation of the recently completed Phase I revealed that less than 1% of the 10,000 participants were persons with disabilities. The current phase, officially launched in July 2025, seeks to increase this representation to approximately 10%. Recruitment of project participants is scheduled to take place between January and March 2026.
In July 2025, CAFOD engaged the Christian Blind Mission (CBM) through the CAFOD Disability Inclusion Helpdesk to review disability inclusion within the Phase II project’s outcomes, outputs, activities, and participant selection criteria. This review primarily involved a desk analysis of project documents, selection criteria, and recruitment processes to enhance inclusivity in participant recruitment and retention. To ensure that women and girls with disabilities are not only eligible but actively and meaningfully included, CBM proposed three key recommendations aimed at strengthening accessibility, representation, and support throughout the selection process.
